data.name: Mukhlas
data.gender_notes: Mukhlas is used as a unisex name in Islamic naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Derived from the Arabic root 'kh-l-s', meaning 'to purify' or 'to cleanse'. In Islamic context, it is often used to describe a person who is sincere and righteous in their beliefs and actions. The name Mukhlas carries the meaning “Pure, Clean” and is chosen by families in Islamic traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Arabic tradition and is also used in Arabic, Urdu, Persian. Parents who choose Mukhlas usually hope their child will grow to embody pure, clean and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Symbolizes the purification of one's soul and the striving for righteousness and closeness to Allah.
data.etymology: Mukhlas belongs to the Arabic linguistic tradition and is used in Islamic naming. Its recorded meaning is “Pure, Clean.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Mukhlas total 4, giving a life-path number of 4. Number 4 is linked with Rahu and with the qualities of stability, discipline and hard work.

in_arabic.name: مخلس
in_arabic.long_meaning: المخلص من الله تعالى هو الشخص الذي يخلص نفسه من الأخطاء والغياب عن الله تعالى، ويحصل على الرضا الله تعالى، ويحصل على النجاح والنجاة في الدنيا والآخرة، ويحصل على الجنة الكرامة والفردوس الأعلى، وهو الشخص الذي يخلص نفسه من الشهوات والطغيان والفساد، ويحصل على الخير والبركة والنجاح والنجاة، ويحصل على العفو والرحمة من الله تعالى، ويحصل على الجنة والفردوس الأعلى.

historical_references.reference: Mukhlas bint Amr ibn Al-As: A prominent companion and wife of Prophet Muhammad (PBUH) who pledged her allegiance to Islam early on. She was a key figure in the Migration to Medina and was one of the first Ansar women to embrace Islam.
historical_references.context: Pre-Islamic Arabia and early Islamic history

historical_references.reference: Mukhlas bint Abu Quhafa: A companion and wife of Prophet Muhammad (PBUH) who was widowed during his last years. She was known for her piety and generosity and is believed to have been one of the first women to wear the hijab in the Prophet's mosque in Medina.
historical_references.context: Late Islamic history and the Prophet's last years
